commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Scrape node metrics from the local kubelet (#8712)

The Kubernetes node agent reads its own kubelet's metrics/resource
endpoint over
loopback instead of routing the request through the apiserver's
nodes/proxy
subresource. Every sample previously crossed the cluster's Konnectivity
tunnel,
the control-plane path that also carries exec, port-forward, and logs.
On
cw-rno2a that was 65 agents at roughly 2.2 requests per second and about
33 KiB
per response, and while the control plane was congested a third of those
requests were failing with 503. After the rollout the cluster's
nodes/proxy rate
measures 0.00/s on a replica-pinned 60-second window, against 776,931
cumulative
requests before it, and task stats keep landing in finelog.

The agent already runs on the host network, so the kubelet is reachable
at
127.0.0.1:10250. The kubelet authorizes that endpoint against the
nodes/metrics
subresource rather than nodes/proxy, so the controller ClusterRole
grants
nodes/metrics; IaC owns that role and renders it from these shared
manifest
builders, so the stacks must be applied before the agents roll or the
new agents
403. The kubelet's serving certificate is issued by the node and does
not verify
against the service-account CA bundle, so the loopback connection does
not
verify it.

The kubernetes client reports transport failures as urllib3 errors
rather than
ApiException, so a read timeout escaped every call site in the k8s
service
wrapper. In the node agent that exception propagated out of the
collection loop
and terminated the process, and the kubelet restarted it straight back
into the
same scrape; agents on cw-rno2a had accumulated 11 to 24 restarts each,
two of
them above 50. A _k8s_call context manager now wraps the existing
slow_log
timing and converts those errors to KubectlError once, naming the
operation for
both the slow-call warning and the raised error. Call sites that select
handling
from a status code keep their own except ApiException; exec keeps a
combined
clause because it reports failure as an ExecResult, and delete_many and
delete_by_labels issue no direct API calls.

The node agent's apiserver timeout moves from 2 to 15 seconds. The
2-second
value was tripping whenever apiserver latency rose, which is what turned
congestion into a restart loop.

Deployed to cw-rno2a, cw-us-east-02a, cw-us-east-08a, and
cw-us-west-04a, each
with a smoke job and, except for CI, a five-minute verify against a
pre-restart
baseline. All four report healthy controllers with node counts
unchanged. The
deployed trees predate the error-translation consolidation, which is
behavior-preserving.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Partition Levanter metrics online (#8707)

Partition `levanter.metrics` by exact `run_id` metadata while keeping L0
flat. Exact run predicates prune current partitions; legacy and
transition files remain visible during online migration. Compacted files
use the bounded directory layout `levanter.metrics/run_id/00..31/`
without weakening the full run-id partition recorded in segment
metadata.

Converge existing local and archived segments without stopping
ingestion. A store-wide two-worker permit bounds rebuild memory, and
namespaces without a physical partition policy stay on ordinary
compaction. `levanter.metrics` intentionally uses no secondary indexes:
managed registration withdraws the inherited telemetry declarations,
readers ignore old bundles, and bounded maintenance removes local
derived files online.

Carry the current execution identity from Hero phase enrollment into
health aggregation and scan `levanter.metrics` once with exact run and
execution predicates. The training run selector now uses a fixed 12-hour
discovery window rather than inheriting the graph window. The former
seven-day selector scanned 1.068 billion rows across 17,411 segments and
exceeded the server's 10-second deadline; production probes of the
bounded selector completed in 2.10–3.58 seconds. Explicitly selected
historical runs remain queryable.

The production migration routed 1,723,699,039 of 2,173,077,173 legacy
rows into semantic telemetry and typed Levanter tables. After Grafana
switched to semantic queries, Finelog returned to normal single-write
mode, accepted a semantic-only canary exactly once, and retired the
compatibility root. Removing the rollback tree and retired local root
files reclaimed about 92 GB; the GCS compatibility archive remains
intact.

The complete Finelog suite passes with 458 tests and one pre-existing
ignored test. The Grafana suite passes all 252 tests. Rust checks,
clippy, repository lint, and required CI checks pass.

https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/256

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[zephyr] Cache shuffle schemas and consolidate merge passes (#8677)

Record each scatter Parquet chunk's Arrow schema alongside its path in
the mapper sidecar. Reducers use those schemas to reconcile merge
inputs, eliminating one object-storage footer read per input during
schema unification while preserving widening for source-shard dtype
drift.

Move the bounded multi-pass merge into `shuffle.py` and use it for
direct and spilling merges. The existing memory decision remains
unchanged: the 0.4 read fraction, both 2× overhead factors,
`ceil(sqrt(total_chunks))` first-pass fan-in, and 32-run cap for later
passes are preserved.

PR [#8204](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8204) replaces
those memory limits with a shared budget model.

An [ad-hoc Datakit Tier 1
ferry](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Floom%2Firis-run-job-20260825-202343)
in `us-central2` completed in 5,820.7 seconds, 2.0% faster than the
[same-day
reference](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frunner%2Firis-run-job-20260825-072626)
at 5,939.7 seconds. Stage wall-time deltas were download +26.1%,
normalize +0.4%, minhash -24.4%, fuzzy deduplication -6.9%, consolidate
+8.4%, and tokenize -6.1%. Aggregate task-seconds increased 14.2%.

Peak worker memory was 4.84 GiB versus 4.82 GiB. Both runs had zero OOMs
and zero failed final shards. All 917 observed treatment tasks ran on
`us-central2-b` scale groups under `MARIN_MIRROR_BUDGET_GB=0`, and the
ferry logs contained no cross-region event. One fuzzy worker exited
after five coordinator heartbeat failures during a phase transition. The
root ferry exited 0.

commits.author: claude[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Split ArrayStacked norm logging by layer (#8689)

Emit per-layer parameter and gradient norms for ArrayStacked when
split_scan_layers is set. summary_statistics_for_tree previously
special-cased
only haliax.nn.Stacked, whose named Block axis it vmaps over. Grug MoE
stacks
its transformer blocks in haliax.nn.ArrayStacked, which stores
layer-batched
plain arrays with a leading num_layers axis and no named Block, so those
trees
fell through to the plain-leaf branch and collapsed the layer axis into
one norm
per stacked parameter. The metric keys carried no layer index, so a
layer with
runaway parameter or gradient growth could not be identified.

ArrayStacked is now treated as a split-scan container: the recursive
norm helper
is vmapped over the leading layer axis (axis 0 for layer-batched leaves,
None for
shared leaves), and each result is indexed to key.{layer}.{name},
matching the
existing Stacked keys.

Fixes #8688

Co-authored-by: claude[bot] <41898282+claude[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[cleanup] Collapse duplicated helpers and delete dead scatter plumbing (#8696)

Consolidate three duplicated definitions and delete one dead statistic.

The GCP slice-bootstrap `/health` poll and the autoscaler's liveness
probe each
carried their own copy of the worker health check, and the copies had
drifted.
The autoscaler opens through a `ProxyHandler({})` opener because worker
addresses are private cluster IPs; the bootstrap copy called
`urllib.request.urlopen`, which consults `HTTP_PROXY`. Both run in the
controller process, so a proxy in the controller environment made
bootstrap
probes fail or hang against private IPs while autoscaler probes worked.
The two
also disagreed on success: 2xx versus exactly 200. The probe now lives
once in
`iris.cluster.platforms.types` beside the other network helpers, keeps
the proxy
bypass and the 2xx check, and takes the per-probe timeout as a required
argument
so each caller retains its value (3 s fanned-out, 5 s serial).

`marin.evaluation.perplexity_gap` held a byte-identical copy of
Levanter's
`_summary_scalars`, so both W&B loggers for the same gap summary owned
their own
`gap/...` metric-key policy; #5337 had to edit the two in lockstep. The
Levanter
function is now public as `gap_summary_scalars` and Marin imports it.
Metric keys
and values are unchanged.

`levanter/store` had two copies of `_render_path_elem` and four inlined
spellings
of the join over it. That joined string is the on-disk layout contract:
`TreeStore` opens each leaf's `JaggedArrayStore` under it and
`CacheLedger.field_counts` is keyed by it, so the copies must agree or
ledger
counts stop naming the stores they describe. `render_tree_path` in
`tree_store.py` now owns it.

Zephyr's scatter `avg_item_bytes` has had no consumer since #5963 moved
the
reducer's external-sort sizing onto the exact per-shard `shard_bytes`.
Every
mapper still accumulated it and wrote it to its `metadata.msgpack`
sidecar, and
every reducer read it back into a file-count-weighted mean that reached
only a
log line — and that mean averaged per-mapper row-averages by file count,
which
is not what the name suggests. The accumulators, sidecar field,
`ScatterReader`
parameter, and derived attribute are gone; `shard_bytes` and the
per-flush
`estimated_size()` behind the GC threshold are untouched.

commits.message:
Drop RunDisabled from the WandbRun type alias (#8693)

wandb deprecated `RunDisabled` in v0.17.6 (wandb/wandb#8064): since
then, `wandb.init(mode="disabled")` returns a regular no-op `wandb.Run`,
and `RunDisabled` has been an empty compatibility shim that emits a
deprecation warning on attribute access. The shim is being removed in an
upcoming wandb release (wandb/wandb#12586), after which importing it
raises `ImportError`.

Details: the `WandbRun` union alias in the vendored levanter tracker
uses a string forward ref to `wandb.sdk.lib.disabled.RunDisabled`; there
is no runtime break, but type checkers would fail to resolve it. The
alias becomes a plain forward ref to `wandb.sdk.wandb_run.Run`.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[iac] Grant Iris job submission to the XLA fork's CI (#8685)

## What changed

One member added to `github-iris@hai-gcp-models`, for
`roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser`:

```
principalSet://.../workloadIdentityPools/github-pool/attribute.repository/marin-community/xla
```

## Why

`marin-community/xla` is Marin's XLA fork. It carries a ragged
all-to-all device-kernel change that expert-parallel MoE training on
GB200 needs and that is not upstream, and it builds a patched
`jax-cuda13-pjrt` wheel.

The fork's CI must run that wheel on a real GB200 before Marin can pin
it. A wheel whose change is inert still passes a correctness test, and
still benchmarks as a null result, so without a hardware check "the
change did not help" and "the change was never present" look the same.
That job submits to Iris, which needs this service account.

The grant matches what the other five fork repositories already have. It
adds no new role and no new pool. It is scoped by
`attribute.repository`, so only workflows running in
`marin-community/xla` can use it.

## Related

- marin-community/xla#1 and marin-community/xla#3 carry the kernel
change and the build.
- marin-community/marin#8684 is the Marin-side pin. It stays in draft
until a validated wheel exists, which is what this grant unblocks.

## For the reviewer

Run `review-grant`, then `pulumi up` on the `marin` stack.

`infra/pulumi/tests` passes with this change: 89 passed, 1 failed. The
12 tests that read `iam_data.yaml` (`test_iam_targets.py`,
`test_iam.py`, `test_iam_config.py`) all pass.

The one failure is
`test_iris_service.py::TestCodeHash::test_content_change_changes_hash`,
which fails identically on unmodified `main`. It is unrelated to IAM:
`code_hash` returns the empty-input digest on both calls, so it never
reads the file contents.

Run them with:

```bash
uv sync --package marin-iac --extra deploy --group test
uv run --package marin-iac --extra deploy --group test pytest infra/pulumi/tests -q
```

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[echo] Expose search timings and reduce rerank latency (#8692)

Report federated-search query embedding, database setup, per-domain
retrieval,
reranking, history persistence, and total application time through the
standard
`Server-Timing` header. The CLI prints these stages beside caller wall
time so
queueing, token acquisition, network delay, and response decoding remain
distinguishable from API execution.

Score the existing 24 INT8 MiniLM candidates one document at a time and
run
ONNX inference with four threads. Move Echo from one always-allocated
1-vCPU
instance accepting four requests to request-based 4-vCPU instances with
one
warm minimum, concurrency one, and a maximum of four. Separate startup
CPU
boost from always-allocated CPU, preserve existing Grafana and EvalDash
behavior explicitly, and use lazy Cloud SQL certificate refresh while
idle CPU
is throttled.

On the reported Finelog query, single-document batches reduced the warm
local
median from 4.32 to 3.78 seconds and reranking from 3.80 to 3.23
seconds. Four
inference threads reduced the exact 24-document rerank further, from
3.26 to
1.01 seconds, for an estimated warm search near 1.6 seconds. Production
hardware
may scale differently, so the new stage timings expose the rollout
result.

A 16-candidate cap kept development hit rate but lost one
answerable-query hit
on the frozen held-out split, so the candidate budget remains 24. INT8
BGE query
embedding saved 32 milliseconds, under 1% of the local baseline, and
would
require a quality evaluation and corpus reindex. Smaller rerankers were
faster
but remain unevaluated on Echo's frozen judgments.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[telemetry] Separate training metrics from service telemetry (#8571)

Levanter produced 66.2% of retained telemetry rows in the measured
production snapshot, while node-agent telemetry contributed 28.0%. A
10.08 GiB replay containing 431,783,340 rows projected a 68.6%
compressed-byte reduction from process-zero publication, lower detail
cadence, and narrower metric selection. Compaction-time downsampling
remains a follow-up: 60-second sampling already moved some five-minute
GPU aggregates, and 300-second sampling degraded them materially.

This separates explicitly collected training metrics from automatically
sampled service telemetry. Levanter now writes typed scalar, summary,
and histogram rows to the canonical `levanter.metrics` table through the
per-run writer name `levanter.metrics.<run_id>`. `run_id` and `step` are
columns; step is no longer a standalone metric row. Finelog stores exact
hidden `run_id` partition metadata in each segment, uses it during
compaction, and prunes partitions for exact run queries without creating
a table or query-provider union per run.

Levanter publishes training metrics only from process zero. Loss, phase,
and progress remain available every step; other scalars and reduced
summaries are emitted every ten steps. Histogram moments and buckets
occupy one typed row rather than many gauge rows. Automatic Levanter
service telemetry, including NCCL RAS, remains under
`telemetry_v1.levanter`. Node-agent collection moves from 30 to 60
seconds, and vLLM and Iris RPC collection move from 15 to 60 seconds.
Histogram sibling coherence remains 15 seconds so historical
high-cadence vLLM samples are not merged when reading the new 60-second
stream.

Finelog now registers ordered ingestion, storage, and physical-partition
policies in `policies.rs`. An ingestion policy receives the complete
record batch and returns logical destinations. Unregistered schemas
retain identity ingestion and default storage. The same telemetry policy
drives live ingestion and migration: old `telemetry_v1` Levanter gauge
rows become typed `levanter.metrics` rows, while automatic service rows
move to semantic tables such as `telemetry_v1.node_agent`,
`telemetry_v1.iris.rpc`, `telemetry_v1.vllm`, and `telemetry_v1.zephyr`.
`/v1/telemetry` has no client-selected group or namespace field.

The legacy root receives a 50 GiB retention budget for rollout breathing
room. Typed Levanter metrics receive 32 GiB; automatic semantic streams
have bounded per-service budgets. Grafana, Iris RPC, vLLM, alerting, and
diagnostic queries now address concrete semantic tables. There is no
root rollup, storage-class name in a client API, or
`priority`/`bulk`/`core`/`extra` namespace.

`finelog-migrate` plans from catalog metadata and Parquet footers,
builds a narrow historical step index, then applies the registered
ingestion and partition policies to full batches. Preparation is
resumable while the server serves traffic. Verification rereads the
source snapshot and staged Parquets, then records a durable marker in
the migration manifest. Publish refuses an unverified manifest; during
the stopped interval it only hard-links the staged files, builds and
swaps the catalog, and checks the catalog rows. Root retirement is a
separate stopped-server catalog cutover with a rollback snapshot.
Finelog forwarders need no special configuration: they forward the
physical tables produced by the edge policy, and the migration refuses
forwarding stores. Rigging treats non-429 HTTP 4xx responses as
permanent rejection, so invalid writes fail visibly rather than
replaying forever.

The corrected local rehearsal used 45,289,841 production rows across
L0/L1 shards. Planning took 21 ms; preparation took 111 seconds with
about 683 MiB peak RSS. It produced 31,101,772 rows, including 8,069,638
typed Levanter rows. Of those, 99.969% carried a reconstructed step; the
remaining 2,503 all preceded the first observed step for their
execution, with zero missing afterward.

The marin-dev rehearsal used a frozen 250 MiB known-good snapshot while
legacy-root writes, direct typed writes, RPC writes, and sample queries
ran throughout deployment and cutover. Planning took 307 ms; preparation
took 69 seconds. All 457 legacy step writes, 457 direct typed step
writes, and 598 acknowledged RPC writes persisted, with no rejected or
lost client records. The root was retired and the corrected typed layout
is serving on marin-dev.

Production publication verified 524 source segments, 53.58 GiB, 2.173
billion input rows, and all 34,286 staged files containing 1.724 billion
routed rows. Stop-to-health publication took 22.295 seconds. Dual-write
remains enabled and the root table remains available for rollback.

The first production query validation found that `levanter.metrics`
inherited the global 1,000-segment cap. Its 12,468 migrated local L0
segments caused each fresh compacted L1 to be offloaded even though the
namespace used only 9.6 GiB of its 32 GiB budget. The namespace now
retains by bytes with an effectively disabled count cap. A bounded
recovery restored 5,399 recent segments totaling 122,781,735 bytes.
Active hero, node-agent, and vLLM probes match exactly between root and
semantic tables. All 61 checked-in semantic-table dashboard queries
completed; maximum query time was 909 ms and maximum planning time was
498 ms. Repeated generated hero-health queries took 2.6–3.2 seconds,
below the 10-second server deadline.

Validation on current main passes Clippy with warnings denied, 446
Finelog library tests with one ignored test, six server-binary tests,
1,522 repository tests with three skips and five expected failures, the
focused Levanter and Grafana suites, repository lint and Pyrefly, and
strict MkDocs.

http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/telemetry-volume-mitigation-analysis

Typed metrics proposal:
http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/levanter-metrics-layout-research

Policy flow:
http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/telemetry-layout-policy-flow

http://127.0.0.1:7878/s/l7xftsek/artifacts/telemetry-policy-rollout-runbook

[levanter] Publish checkpoint phase telemetry (#8663)

Publish checkpoint phase duration, total duration, staged host bytes,
and process peak RSS to Finelog when checkpoint debug mode is enabled.
The numeric series make synchronous staging and asynchronous commit time
available without parsing task logs.

Each JAX process reports its local phases. Process zero reports total
duration after the distributed barrier and metadata commit. Nonprimary
progress loggers stop after their local TensorStore commits finish.

Document a configuration that disables `tracemalloc`, forced garbage
collection, allocation reports, and forced log output. The stacked hero
diagnostic launcher exposes this configuration through
`--checkpoint-debug` for a bounded checkpoint smoke test. The reference
includes a bounded regional Finelog query.

Three one-rack GB200 runs used the 535B model, synthetic data, batch 64,
and two training steps. Normal-step throughput changed from -0.1% to
+5.1% across two debug runs. Post-checkpoint throughput decreased by
83.5% and 87.9% against the no-debug control. In the last matched pair,
duration increased from 10.17 seconds to 84.02 seconds. These results
limit debug mode to bounded diagnostics until its checkpoint-path cost
is removed.

[levanter] Add merged cache catalogs (#8472)

Opening hundreds of cache-backed mixture components currently requires
one ledger read per component. Add a versioned catalog that embeds each
named cache path and ledger by split, and let `LmDataConfig` load that
catalog once as the authoritative cache snapshot. Catalog creation
includes components whose current training weight is zero so later jobs
can choose mixture frequencies at runtime. Required training components
missing from the snapshot fail before dataset construction; optional
validation entries may be omitted.

Existing cache stores can gain a catalog by rolling up their ledgers
without rewriting token data. New Zarr arrays use an explicit Blosc Zstd
level 1 write codec. Readers rely on each array's persisted Zarr
metadata, so existing LZ4 caches remain readable; converting their
chunks to Zstd still requires a data rewrite.

An Iris benchmark on `cw-rno2a` reading and writing `marin-us-east-02a`
used 300 components with ten shards each. The 312,034-byte catalog took
2.89 seconds to build once. Median startup fell from 1.886 seconds for
individual ledgers to 0.485 seconds for the catalog, a 3.89x speedup.

The same job wrote and fully read 256 MiB of Zipf-distributed token IDs.
Zstd level 1 stored 86,990,443 bytes versus 114,189,567 bytes for LZ4
level 5, a 23.8% reduction. Median write time fell from 3.114 to 3.010
seconds, and median read time fell from 1.117 to 1.038 seconds. Each
codec had two repetitions with visible cold/warm spread, so the
throughput comparison is directional; the stored-byte reduction is the
stronger result. The benchmark is reproducible with
`scripts/levanter_cache_benchmark.py`; Iris job
`/app/levanter-cache-benchmark-20260820-154341` completed successfully.

The focused cache and text suites pass all 65 tests. After rebasing onto
`main`, the affected-test selector passes 657 tests with 6 skips.
Changed-file lint, formatting, and type checks pass.

[canary] Allow TPU ferry launcher on preemptible capacity (#8630)

Allow the TPU ferry's small CPU launcher to prefer preemptible capacity
while retaining on-demand fallback.

[Scheduled run
32699287522](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/32699287522)
requested v5p-8 availability. Iris also inferred a required
non-preemptible constraint for the one-core launcher. The only two v5p-8
groups were preemptible, so no scaling group satisfied both constraints
and submission ended before Iris returned a job ID.

The explicit preference suppresses that executor inference. The existing
v5p-8 reservation continues to select a region where the TPU child can
run. Changed-file checks and seven focused Iris constraint and scheduler
tests pass.
